General
* The task currently lacks any key programming elements such as lists, sets, dictionaries, string manipulation, loops, conditions…

Please include one or more programming elements so that the task is a programming one rather than a purely maths one.

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement using the syntax shown on that page (<<bold>> for line numbers, [[variable]] for variable names).

Thanks.
Thank you for your suggestion.I'm changing it.

Formatting (Input, Output and Constraints sections)
* See my last comment; use <<bold>> for line numbers, [[variable]] for variable names,
{{constants}} for the symbols.

General
* This is optional, but I recommend to replace the standard operators with letters or other symbols to make the clash slightly harder. As it stands, players using languages with an eval function (such as Python or JavaScript) can theoretically solve the task in under 20 seconds. For example, in Python, they could simply replace the last line of the default code with:

print(int(eval(f"{a}{s}{b}")))

If you replace +, -, *, /, and % with symbols such as u, v, w, x, and y, those players would at least need to write a less straightforward solution. This also makes Shortest mode more interesting.

Goal
* Please replace "rational number" with "integers" to be precise.

* Please replace "operation symbol in a string format" with "operator".

* Please rewrite the second sentence as:

Your task is to output the result of applying the operator to the two integers. The operator will be one of the following:

{{+}}: addition
{{-}}: subtraction
{{*}}: multiplication
{{/}}: division
{{%}}: modulo

Input
* Line 1: Please change "rational number" to "An integer for the first operand". The variable name "a" should be formatted.

* Line 2: Similar to Line 1.

* Line 3: Please rewrite as:
<<Line 3>>: A string [[s]] representing the operator.

Output
* Please replace "the operation value of two numbers" with "An integer representing the result".

Constraints
* The third constraint can be removed after listing the possible operators in the Goal section.

* Please add:
When [[s]] is {{/}}, [[a]] is an integer multiple of [[b]].
When [[s]] is {{/}} and {{%}}, [[b]] ≠ 0.

Game modes
* Consider enabling the Fastest mode if you replace the standard operators as suggested above.

Cases
* Each test and its validator should cover the same scenario, differing only slightly in their inputs and outputs. Currently, the pairs don't match. For example, Test 1 covers +, while Validator 1 covers %.

Please revise the cases so that each test covers the same operator as its validator (i.e. at least 5 case pairs in total).

Note: You're not limited to 4 test/validator pairs.

* Please avoid inputs where replacing the operator with a different one would produce the same output, as such cases don't verify that the correct operator has been applied (and also cause issues in Reverse mode if the standard operators are replaced). For example:

  • Test 1: 2 2 + (same as 2 2 *)

  • Test 4: 201 199 % (same as 201 199 -)

* There's currently only one case where [[b]] is negative. There are no cases where [[a]] is negative, nor any that expect a negative output. Please include at least one test/validator pair for each of the following scenarios:

  • [[a]] is positive and [[b]] is negative.

  • [[a]] is negative and [[b]] is positive.

  • [[a]] and [[b]] are both negative.

  • The output is negative.

Thanks.
Thank you for your advice.I will consider it seriously.
